chunks: And he also narrated from Hammad ibn Isa from Hariz from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and Jamil from Zurarah from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

There are not two Umras in one year. The resolution between these two narrations is that there are not two Umras in the year with which one performs Tamattu' to Hajj. As for the Umra al-Mabtulah (the independent Umra) with which one does not perform Tamattu' to Hajj, it is permissible in every month, indeed in every ten days.
ai.seo_question: How many Umras can be performed in a single year according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi resolves the apparent contradiction in the hadith by distinguishing between Umra al-Tamattu' (the ritual Umra performed specifically for Hajj) and Umra al-Mabtulah (an independent, non-Hajj Umra). He establishes that while only one Umra al-Tamattu' is permitted per year, Umra al-Mabtulah is not restricted and may be performed multiple times, even every ten days, highlighting the flexibility in Shia jurisprudence regarding voluntary pilgrimage.
